text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated DNS resolution error rate seen from Cloudflare public resolvers (1.1.1.1 family) impacting geo-routing decisions for eu-west and eu-central. Detection: 08:42 UTC, spike in SERVFAIL and timeouts. Affected endpoints: api.redwood.example.com (geo-dns), model-serving endpoints behind geodns. Graph: https://prom.redwood/graph/xyz (reaction :rotating_light:)

maria_sre: ack. i'm oncall. paging network team and eng. i'll take lead for mitigation.

tom_net: on it. seeing increased rcode=SERVFAIL from 1.1.1.1 in EU PoPs, TTL still 60s for geo records. probes show inconsistent answers across CF resolvers vs Route53.

maria_sre: can you paste a dig from eu-west probe?

tom_net:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11 <<>> @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.example.com A +short +time=4
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached

; <<>> DiG 9.11 <<>> @52.95.0.1 api.redwood.example.com A +short +time=20
52.95.123.10
```

maria_sre: thanks. same from our internal resolver probes - cloudflare resolvers returning SERVFAIL or no answer intermittently. Route53 authoritative is healthy.

oliver_eng: support team reporting customer error spikes for users in EU (failed model inference calls, 5xx from edge). CS is seeing tickets.

aj_support: confirmed. CS notes about 18 customers reporting degraded request rates starting ~08:41 UTC. no data exfiltration. customer-facing services degraded ~12% P50 latency increase + 5xx spike for ~10% of EU traffic.

lena_cs: filing incident banner draft now. suggested: "We are investigating increased request failures affecting some customers in EU regions. Engineers are working on mitigation."

maria_sre: mitigation plan:
1) reduce geodns record TTL to 10s (so we can steer faster)
2) adjust geo-routing policy to prefer Route53-backed pool for EU (manual override)
3) add resolver fallback: prefer 52.95.0.1 (our internal resolver/route53) for edge caches
4) open ticket with Cloudflare and provide probe logs
5) monitor error rate; rollback if errors increase

tom_net: lowering TTL now.

incident-bot: ACTION: terraform apply started to update geodns TTL and weights (run_id: tf-9823)

maria_sre: applied weight shift to favor route53 pool by 80% for eu-west and eu-central. watch for propagation.

tom_net: verifying with probes...
```
# after weight change
dig @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.example.com +short
# <no consistent answer>

dig @52.95.0.1 api.redwood.example.com +short
52.95.123.10
```

oliver_eng: edge caches starting to route more traffic to route53 answers. error rate down from ~18% -> ~4% in last 60s. continue monitoring.

aj_support: updated customers on mitigation. CS says two enterprise customers asked for postmortem and SLA credit assessment.

cloudflare-agent: (external) we've received a ticket from Redwood (INC-54321). Initial triage shows internal upstream routing flap affecting some resolvers in EU. We're routing to the resolver team.

maria_sre: good. keep in touch. also enabling temporary H2 keepalive reduction on egress for EU to reduce retry noise.

oliver_eng: rolling h2 keepalive change to edge proxies (canary 10% -> 50%). watch span traces for improvement.

incident-bot: METRIC_UPDATE: dns_query_fail_rate_eu peaked 0.18 at 08:42 UTC, now 0.035 at 08:56 UTC. request_error_rate_eu decreased accordingly.

maria_sre: current status: partial mitigation succeeded. residual errors ~3-4% concentrated to specific CF resolver IP ranges. cs to track customers for possible follow-up.

lena_cs: banner up: "Investigating increased request failures in EU. Mitigation in progress."

aj_support: logging all affected customer ids into a ticket and flagging for SLA review.

maria_sre: next steps: keep Cloudflare ticket open, request their resolver-level logs, set longer-term plan: add health-check-based geodns failover to add automatic failback triggers. assign postmortem to SRE/Network.

oliver_eng: capturing config changes in incident runbook. TF changes: geodns weights and TTL changed. pushing emergency rollback stub.

maria_sre: thanks everyone. i'll hand off to night oncall in 30m with summary.

maria_sre: SUMMARY: Root cause appears to be Cloudflare resolver instability in EU PoPs causing inconsistent authoritative responses to geo DNS lookup. Mitigation: manually weighted traffic to Route53 pool and reduced TTL to accelerate steering. Impact: ~10-20% of EU traffic experienced elevated 5xx/latency, now reduced to ~3-4%. Customer outreach and postmortem scheduled.

tom_net: leaving notes in incident channel and adding dig + mtr traces to ticket.

incident-bot: NOTE: oncall handoff scheduled at 09:25 UTC to @jason_sre (night).

maria_sre: handing off. will follow up in postmortem. closing incident thread after postmortem created.
